problem.paragraph: Suppose a curve is given by the parametric equations $$x = f(t)$$ , $$y = g(t)$$ , where the range of $$f$$ is $$\left\lbrack {1,4} \right\rbrack$$ and the range of $$g$$ is $$\left\lbrack {2,3} \right\rbrack$$ . What can you say about the curve?

solution.paragraph: It is contained in the rectangle described by $$1 \leqslant x \leqslant 4$$ and $$2 \leqslant y \leqslant 3$$ .

problem.paragraph: Investigate the family of curves defined by the parametric equations $$x = t^{2}$$ , $$y = t^{3} - ct$$ . How does the shape change as $$c$$ increases? Illustrate by graphing several members of the family.

solution.paragraph: For $$c = 0$$ , there is a cusp; for $$c > 0$$ , there is a loop whose size increases as $$c$$ increases.

problem.paragraph: The swallowtail catastrophe curves are defined by the parametric equations $$x = 2ct - 4t^{3}$$ , $$y = - ct^{2} + 3t^{4}$$ . Graph several of these curves. What features do the curves have in common? How do they change when $$c$$ increases?

Graph several members of the family of curves with parametric equations $$x = t + a\cos t$$ , $$y = t + a\sin t$$ , where $$a > 0$$ . How does the shape change as $$a$$ increases? For what values of $$a$$ does the curve have a loop?

solution.paragraph: The curves roughly follow the line $$y = x$$ and start having loops when $$a$$ is between $$1.4$$ and $$1.6$$ (more precisely, when $$a > \sqrt{2}$$ ); the loops increase in size as $$a$$ increases.

problem.paragraph: Graph several members of the family of curves $$x = \sin t + \sin nt$$ , $$y = \cos t + \cos nt$$ , where $$n$$ is a positive integer. What features do the curves have in common? What happens as $$n$$ increases?

The curves with equations $$x = a\sin nt$$ , $$y = b\cos t$$ are called Lissajous figures. Investigate how these curves vary when $$a$$ , $$b$$ , and $$n$$ vary. (Take $$n$$ to be a positive integer.)

solution.paragraph: As $$n$$ increases, the number of oscillations increases; $$a$$ and $$b$$ determine the width and height.

problem.paragraph: Investigate the family of curves defined by the parametric equations $$x = \cos t$$ , $$y = \sin t - \sin ct$$ , where $$c > 0$$ . Start by letting $$c$$ be a positive integer and see what happens to the shape as $$c$$ increases. Then explore some of the possibilities that occur when $$c$$ is a fraction.
